text:
Gavin McKenna arrived in Toronto as the first overall pick and the most talked-about prospect in years, and his first six weeks have been a lesson in how the NHL meters out ice time. He's playing 13:55 a night, mostly sheltered, with the power play doing a lot of the lifting: seven of his 13 points in 22 games have come with the man advantage. As the Leafs have slid through a losing run, his minutes have been squeezed (10:36 against Minnesota), and the headlines this week were about him talking openly about playing less.

Our numbers back the caution at even strength. Toronto gets 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five-on-five with him on the ice, and his own chances are modest so far. He's shooting 16.7%, a bit above where we'd expect it to settle. The tools are obvious, though: his top skating speed sits in the 97th percentile of the league, at 18. His pace of 0.59 points a game is right around the 0.55 median for forwards picked in the top three, which is about what a normal rookie year looks like. Watch his five-on-five minutes; that's where the trust shows.
